review_time_definition: Wall-clock from first detailed inspection to submission; includes coordination/tool delays, not independent human labor.

anchors.quote: Conditionally encode the indices from col through n-1 as a finite search domain. For fixed augmented-row state, mark the unique index whose absolute active-column value is strictly greater than every earlier candidate's value and at least every later candidate's value, thereby reproducing Python max's first-index tie rule. Use Grover-style search only to propose that pivot index.

Encode col, candidate indices, and the dynamically updated binary64 values rows[i][col]. A reversible oracle must reproduce the relevant Python float absolute-value, comparison, equality, ordering, and first-tie behavior. Coherent access to the augmented rows, representation of signed zero and any nonfinite intermediate state, ancilla cleanup, and gate costs remain unresolved.

Measure a proposed index and classically verify that it equals Python's first-index argmax under abs(rows[i][col]). On verification failure or unsuccessful quantum execution, use the original classical max expression. Preserve the exact-zero pivot check, row swap, elimination order, back substitution, overflow detection, exceptions, and caller-visible report construction.
Inputs begin as validated finite binary64 values, while the candidate consumes dynamically updated elimination state whose exact representational behavior must be preserved.

binding.rationale: This revision supplies strict greater-than against earlier candidates and at-least against later candidates, unlike the initial >=-all predicate that included self. Nonfinite encoding is unresolved but no executable finite-only admission condition is declared. Bind the literal earlier/later predicate with guard True; fixed row state does not mean finite-valued state. Declared verification and fallback do not establish the local predicate or complete migration.

interpretations.meaning: Candidate strictly exceeds every earlier absolute pivot and is at least every later absolute pivot, with no stated state exclusion.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] > values[j] for j in indices if j < i) and all(values[i] >= values[k] for k in indices if k > i)
